names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιος Μνάσων ο αρχαίος μαθητής», with the rank words left off. The epithet «ο αρχαίος μαθητής» is Acts 21:16's own phrase for him and is kept in the display name.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιος Μνάσων ο αρχαίος μαθητής»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. A long and careful life, built on Acts 21:15–16 and on his synaxarion and his Service («Ακολουθία αγίου Μνάσωνος σελ. 16, Ενετίησιν 1774»): born at Tamasos in Cyprus of idolatrous parents, sent to Rome with his friend Theonas over a quarrel between the idolaters of Politiko and the village of Pera, taught about Christ there by some of the Seventy, baptised at Jerusalem by John the Theologian, a companion and helper of Heraclides the first bishop of Tamasos, his successor in that see, and dead on 19 October in deep old age three days after ordaining Rhodon in his place. **No `dates`**: the page gives not one year for him, only the apostolic generation and a Russian pilgrim's visit of 1735 to the monastery that later stood by his tomb. No `locations`, the folder being undated. The page prints no hymn. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιος Μνάσων επίσκοπος Κύπρου»

attestations.note: The second Greek day, kept as «Άγιος Μνάσων επίσκοπος Κύπρου» — Mnason bishop of Cyprus, the see given as the island rather than as Tamasos. Its whole notice is one sentence and a conjecture: «Ο Άγιος Μνάσων επίσκοπος Κύπρου μαρτύρησε δια ξίφους», martyred by the sword, and then «Είναι πιθανόν να είναι ο ίδιος Άγιος που εορτάζει στις 19 Οκτωβρίου σαν Άγιος Μνάσων ο αρχαίος μαθητής, παρόλο που εκείνος κοιμήθηκε εν ειρήνη» — it is possible he is the same saint kept on 19 October as Mnason the ancient disciple, although that one fell asleep in peace. **The author ruled on 3 October 2026 that they are one man** and this record is the merge of the two folders the corpus held; the page's own «πιθανόν» and the disagreement about the manner of death are in the life, unresolved, because the source has not resolved them. The `martyr` type comes from this day and the `wonderworker` from the other. Read 2 October 2026; no year, no place beyond the see, no hymn, no asterisk.
